item.title: High Protein Shakshuka: A Budget Dinner That Actually Fills You Up
item.description:
Shakshuka is one of those meals that looks way more impressive than the effort it takes. This version clocks in at 32g of protein per serving and costs around $2.30 a plate, thanks to eggs, canned chickpeas, and a little feta doing the heavy lifting. It’s ready in 30 minutes and works just as well for dinner as it does for a weekend brunch.

Why This Recipe Works
#

Eggs are one of the cheapest protein sources you can buy, and pairing them with chickpeas doubles the protein without adding much cost. The spiced tomato base is deeply flavorful from pantry staples you already have on hand. This is a one-pan meal, which means less cleanup and more time enjoying your food.

item.title: High Protein Lentil Soup: Cheap, Filling, and Perfect for Meal Prep
item.description:
This lentil soup is one of the hardest-working recipes on this blog. Each serving clocks in at 27 grams of protein and costs you roughly $1.75, and one big batch covers your lunches for the entire week. If you’re trying to hit your protein goals without blowing your grocery budget, this one belongs in your regular rotation.

Why This Recipe Works
#

Lentils are an absolute steal at around $1.50 per pound, and they’re loaded with plant-based protein and fiber that keeps you full for hours. Pairing them with canned chickpeas bumps the protein even higher without adding much cost. The whole pot comes together in about 40 minutes with zero fancy equipment required.

item.title: High Protein Meals Under 500 Calories: 5 Budget Recipes to Hit Your Goals
item.description:
Eating high protein on a budget sounds hard until you see what a can of chickpeas, a pound of ground turkey, or a bag of lentils can actually do for you. This post breaks down one of our favorite go-to meals that delivers 35g of protein, stays under 450 calories, and costs about $2.10 per serving. Let’s get into it.

Why This Recipe Works
#

Ground turkey and black beans are one of the best budget protein combos you can build a meal around. Turkey is lean, affordable, and absorbs whatever seasoning you throw at it, and black beans add fiber and extra protein without adding much fat or cost. This is the kind of meal you can make on a Sunday and eat four times during the week without getting bored.

item.title: High Protein Chicken Banh Mi Bowl (Under $3 a Serving)
item.description:
If you love banh mi but hate spending $12 at a sandwich shop, this bowl is your new best friend. It packs 38 grams of protein per serving and costs less than $3 to make at home. Bright, fresh, and filling, this one earns a permanent spot in your meal prep rotation.

Why This Recipe Works
#

Ground chicken is one of the cheapest high-protein options at the grocery store, and it soaks up a simple soy-ginger marinade beautifully. Serving it over rice instead of a baguette keeps costs down without sacrificing any of the flavor you love about classic banh mi. The quick-pickled carrots and cucumbers do a lot of heavy lifting here, giving you that punchy, tangy bite with almost zero effort.

item.title: White Bean and Turkey Chili: High-Protein, Budget-Friendly, and Ready in 30 Minutes
item.description:
If you want a filling, protein-packed meal that doesn’t wreck your grocery budget, this white bean and turkey chili is your new go-to. Each serving clocks in at 32 grams of protein for about $2.30, and the whole pot comes together in under 30 minutes. Meal prep dream, honestly.

Why This Recipe Works
#

Ground turkey is one of the leanest, most affordable proteins you can buy, and canned white beans add a serious protein and fiber boost without adding much cost at all. The combination gives you a thick, hearty chili that actually keeps you full for hours. It also reheats perfectly, so it works great for lunch or dinner throughout the week.

item.title: Slow Cooker Chicken Thighs: High-Protein Meal Prep for Under $3
item.description:
If you want juicy, fall-apart chicken ready to eat all week without spending more than $2.50 a serving, this is your recipe. Each serving packs 38 grams of protein and takes about 10 minutes of actual hands-on work. Let the slow cooker do the rest.

Why This Recipe Works
#

Bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs are one of the cheapest cuts at the grocery store, and they shine in a slow cooker because the fat keeps them moist over a long cook. You get big flavor with minimal effort, and the leftovers reheat beautifully for lunches and dinners all week. No dry chicken, no complicated prep.

item.title: Budget Chicken Thigh Meal Prep: 40g Protein for Under $2.50 a Serving
item.description:
Bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs are one of the best kept secrets in budget meal prep. This recipe gets you four solid meals with 40 grams of protein each, all for around $2.50 per serving. It pairs seasoned oven-baked thighs with rice and roasted broccoli, and the whole thing comes together in about an hour.

Why This Recipe Works
#

Chicken thighs cost significantly less per pound than chicken breasts, and they stay juicy even after reheating, which makes them ideal for meal prep. The simple spice rub builds real flavor without requiring anything fancy. Pairing them with rice and broccoli gives you a complete, balanced meal that reheats well every single day of the week.

item.title: High Protein Chicken Burrito Bowl Under $3
item.description:
If you want 38 grams of protein for under three bucks, this chicken burrito bowl is your new go-to. It’s filling, flavorful, and comes together in about 30 minutes with ingredients you can grab at any grocery store.

Why This Recipe Works
#

Boneless skinless chicken thighs are one of the cheapest high-protein proteins you can buy, often running less than $2 per pound. Pair them with canned black beans and rice, and you get a complete, satisfying meal that keeps you full for hours. The seasoning blend does the heavy lifting so this never tastes like a budget meal.

item.title: Budget Black Bean Tacos: 26g of Protein for Under $2 a Serving
item.description:
These black bean tacos are proof that hitting your protein goals doesn’t require chicken breast at every meal. Each serving clocks in at 26 grams of protein and costs less than $2.00, and you can have dinner on the table in under 20 minutes.

Why This Recipe Works
#

Black beans combined with Greek yogurt and cotija cheese stack up a serious amount of protein without any meat involved. Everything here is a pantry staple or a cheap grocery store find, so there’s no specialty shopping required. It’s fast, filling, and easy to scale up for meal prep.

item.title: Budget Ground Turkey Meal Prep Bowls (35g Protein, Under $2.50 a Serving)
item.description:
If you want to hit your protein goals without burning through your grocery budget, ground turkey is one of the best tools you have. These meal prep bowls come in at around $2.40 per serving and deliver 35 grams of protein each. Make a batch on Sunday and you have lunch or dinner covered for most of the week.

Why This Recipe Works
#

Ground turkey is lean, cheap, and takes on seasoning incredibly well. Paired with brown rice and black beans, you get a complete protein profile plus enough fiber and carbs to keep you full for hours. Everything cooks in under 30 minutes and reheats perfectly, which makes it a no-brainer for weekly prep.

item.title: Cottage Cheese Bowl Ideas: High-Protein Meal Prep for Under $3
item.description:
Cottage cheese bowls are one of the easiest ways to hit your protein goals without touching your wallet. Each bowl comes in at around 30 grams of protein and costs under $2.50 per serving. If you’ve been sleeping on cottage cheese, this post is your wake-up call.

Why This Recipe Works
#

Cottage cheese is a powerhouse ingredient: high protein, low cost, and endlessly versatile. You can build a savory bowl, a sweet bowl, or anything in between using simple pantry staples you already have. It also stores well in the fridge for four to five days, making it one of the best meal prep options out there.

item.title: High Protein Meals Under 500 Calories: Chicken and Rice Power Bowl
item.description:
This chicken and rice power bowl hits 38g of protein per serving, comes in under 450 calories, and costs about $2.30 to make. It meal preps like a dream and uses ingredients you can grab at any grocery store without blowing your budget.

Why This Recipe Works
#

Boneless skinless chicken thighs are one of the cheapest high-protein proteins you can buy, usually around $2 per pound. Paired with brown rice and black beans, you get a complete amino acid profile plus enough fiber to keep you full for hours. This is the kind of meal that makes hitting your protein goals feel effortless.

item.title: Best Protein Sources Under $1 Per Serving (And How to Cook Them)
item.description:
Hitting your protein goals doesn’t have to drain your wallet. These budget protein sources each cost under $1 per serving and deliver 25 grams of protein or more, making them the backbone of any smart meal prep routine. We’re building a simple, satisfying High-Protein Egg and Lentil Bowl that costs about $0.85 per serving and packs in 32 grams of protein.

Why This Recipe Works
#

Eggs and lentils are two of the most protein-dense, affordable foods you can buy at any grocery store. Lentils bring fiber and plant-based protein while eggs add complete amino acids and healthy fat to keep you full longer. Together they create a balanced, filling meal that works for breakfast, lunch, or dinner.

item.title: High Protein Overnight Oats with Greek Yogurt (30g Protein, Under $2)
item.description:
If you want a breakfast that practically makes itself and keeps you full until lunch, this is it. These high protein overnight oats with Greek yogurt pack 30 grams of protein per serving and cost less than $2 to make. Prep five jars on Sunday and your mornings are sorted for the week.

Why This Recipe Works
#

Greek yogurt and cottage cheese team up to push the protein way past what oats alone can offer, without any protein powder required. Everything gets mixed in the jar, sits overnight, and is ready to grab from the fridge in the morning. It is genuinely one of the easiest high-protein meals you can add to your routine.

item.title: Overnight Chocolate Cheesecake Oats (60g Protein, $2.50 a Serving)
item.description:
If you want a meal prep breakfast that actually tastes like dessert and still hits your protein goals hard, this is it. These overnight chocolate cheesecake oats pack 60g of protein per serving and cost around $2.50 each. Six servings, one prep session, done for the week.

Why This Recipe Works
#

The combination of Greek yogurt, protein powder, and gelatin creates a thick, creamy texture that firms up overnight into something that genuinely resembles cheesecake filling. Cacao powder and a crumbled Oreo on top make it feel indulgent without wrecking your macros. It requires zero cooking and about ten minutes of actual work.

item.title: Budget Chicken Burrito Bowl (High Protein, Under $3 a Serving)
item.description:
If you want a filling, high-protein meal that doesn’t wreck your grocery budget, this burrito bowl is it. We’re talking 42 grams of protein per serving for about $2.40, and it comes together in under 30 minutes. It’s also one of the best meals you can batch cook for the week.

Why This Recipe Works
#

Chicken thighs are cheaper than breasts and stay juicy even after reheating, which makes them ideal for meal prep. Canned black beans add a solid protein and fiber boost for almost nothing. Rice stretches everything out so you stay full for hours without spending more.

item.title: Hot Honey Ground Beef Bowl (34g Protein, Under $2.50)
item.description:
If you only make one high-protein budget recipe this week, make this one. Four servings, 20 minutes, 34 grams of protein per bowl, and it costs about $2.30 a serving. The hot honey glaze turns basic ground beef into something that genuinely tastes like it came from a restaurant.

Jump to Recipe

Why This Recipe Works
#

Ground beef is one of the cheapest proteins per gram you can buy. The hot honey glaze — just honey, red pepper flakes, and a splash of vinegar — caramelises against the hot pan and creates little crispy edges on the beef that add real texture. Avocado and rice round it out into a complete, satisfying meal that keeps you full for hours.
